people whose excess fat is located in their lower body (hips,
buttocks, and thighs) seem to have minimal or no increased
risk of these diseases.  Upper-body obesity also is associated
with an increased risk for coronary artery disease, stroke, and
certain cancers.
Therefore, it can be helpful to assess your health risk by
measuring your waist circumference.  A measurement of
more than 35 inches in women and 40 inches in men is
associated with increased health risks, especially if you have
a BMI of 25 or more.
